data.content_ref: inline:The target attempts to ground its distinction between idempotent and safe operations in RFC 9110 by stating that the asymmetry 'maps to RFC 9110's separation of methods into those that change state (PUT, POST, DELETE) and those that don't (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS).' However, this framing fails to precisely distinguish idempotent from safe as required, because it conflates all state-changing methods as a single group. In RFC 9110, the key distinction is that PUT and DELETE change state but are idempotent, whereas POST changes state and is explicitly NOT idempotent. By grouping POST with PUT and DELETE under the umbrella of 'change state' (and implicitly contrasting them with safe methods), the target misclassifies POST and obscures the very definition it was asked to draw out.
